### Observed differences

- The clearest difference is how often a fixed activity chain runs. In the earlier window, A19, A20 and A25 each appeared in about 48 in 100 traces (roughly 95 of 200); in the later window they appear in essentially every trace (199–200 of 200), about once per case with almost no repetition. A14, A15, A16, A26 and A41, by contrast, already appeared in every trace in both windows. [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, REL001, REL002, REL003, POS002]
- When they run, these activities form the sequence A41 → A19 → A25 → A20 → A26. In the later window that order holds in about 97–99 in 100 of the traces where each pair occurs, with the activities one step apart: from A41, A19 follows at distance 1 in about 98 in 100 cases, A25 at distance 2 in about 96, A20 at distance 3 in about 95, and A26 at distance 4 in about 93. In the earlier window A41 was followed directly by A26 at distance 1 in about 46 in 100 cases, and now under 1 in 100 of A41's outgoing transitions go directly to A26 — consistent with the three activities now running between them. [REL018, REL019, REL021, REL022, REL023, LAG018, LAG019, LAG020, LAG021, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006]
- A06 is executed far more often and earlier: participation rose from about 24 to about 73 in 100 traces (47 vs 146 of 200), and its median relative position moved from about 0.39 to about 0.21. Its routing collapsed onto a single successor: before, its outgoing transitions were spread over many activities (largest shares A15 about 21%, A47 about 15%, A45 about 13%); in the later window about 88 in 100 go to A16, immediately (distance 1) in about 97 in 100 of the observed pairs. A06 now precedes A41, A19, A20, A25 and A26 in about 65 in 100 traces. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, LAG002, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008]
- Feeder routing into A06 increased: the share of A15's outgoing transitions going to A06 rose from about 1 to about 40 in 100 (A15 → A16 fell from about 94 to about 58), and A14 now precedes A06 in about 69 in 100 traces (previously about 22), typically two steps earlier. [DIR003, REL001, REL002, LAG006, LAG009]
- A08 is executed less often: about 8 in 100 traces in the later window versus about 20 before (15 vs 40 of 200), and its share of A14's outgoing transitions fell from about 4% to under 1%. [OCC002, DIR002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that in the later window the segment A41 → A19 → A25 → A20 → A26 is executed in essentially every case, whereas in the earlier window it ran in only about half of the cases, with A19, A20 and A25 skipped in the rest. The order within the segment is unchanged — in the earlier window, whenever the activities co-occurred they already followed this sequence — so the difference is how often the block executes, not a reordering: it now runs once per case between A41 and A26, lengthening the A41→A26 distance from about one step to about four. In the same direction, A06 now participates in about three quarters of the cases (previously about a quarter), placed earlier and almost always followed immediately by A16, with more cases entering it from A14 and A15, while A08 participates in fewer cases. The volume of agreeing evidence (62 items versus roughly 1 expected without any change) and its consistency across occurrence, routing, relation and distance indicators fit one coherent shift. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, REL018, REL019, REL021, REL022, LAG018, LAG019, LAG020, LAG021, DIR001, DIR003, DIR006, POS001]

The supporting signs are direct: the participation jump rests on large support (about 95–96 of 200 traces before versus 199–200 after for A19, A20 and A25), the pairwise order and step-distance measurements agree across many activity pairs, and the routing consolidations (A06 → A16, A41 → A19, A15 → A06) move in the same direction as the relational evidence. [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, REL004, REL020, REL025, LAG002, LAG018, LAG021, DIR001, DIR006]

Limitations remain: the two windows are finite samples, so a shift in the variant mix — the earlier window under-representing traces containing the block — is a competing explanation that cannot be fully excluded, even though a difference of about 96 versus 199 of 200 traces is difficult to produce by sampling alone. The many pair-level items largely describe this one underlying shift and are not independent confirmations. Also, A06's exact placement is only partly pinned down: in roughly a third of the later traces it is interleaved or repeated with A15 and A16 rather than occupying one fixed position, and the evidence cannot distinguish whether the block became part of every case or the case mix moved toward traces containing it. [REL002, REL003, REL012, REL015, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005]
